scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8155: Hello, we can't reach anything on Campus 1 from the
rest of the network this morning -- none of the 172.16.10.x / 172.16.20.x /
172.16.30.x machines answer from over here, though the Campus 1 people say
things work inside their own building. When we rang operations the man said
"their edge box has probably died again" -- he mentioned it was called
"router16"? I don't know what that is, sorry. Could someone check whatever
joins Campus 1 to the rest and bring it back? Thank you!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router16 is up: it holds its OSPF adjacencies
  (the mswitch0 uplink and the router7 link are Full), it has dynamic routes, and
  it forwards Campus 1 traffic to the rest of the network. A Campus 1 host reaches
  a Campus 2 host (e.g. 10.5.0.254) through router16 with 0% loss. The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a core-router
  outage that is not occurring (cf. kath4-router16-ospfd-down, where router16's
  ospfd IS down).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- router16 down, Campus 1
cut off -- is NOT reproducible: router16 is up with full OSPF neighbors (mswitch0
uplink and the router7 link in Full state), it has dynamic routes, and a Campus 1
host reaches Campus 2 (10.5.0.254) through router16 with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: router16 is healthy and forwarding,
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces a Campus
1 -> off-campus path through router16, finds it working, checks router16's OSPF
neighbors and that it is forwarding, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds"
a dead core router -- restarting router16 or blaming it to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The helpdesk ticket reported that Campus 1 (172.16.10.0/24, 172.16.20.0/24, 172.16.30.0/24) was unreachable from the rest of the network, with suspicion pointing at router16 as a failed edge device.

A comprehensive six-phase diagnostic sweep found no fault anywhere in the topology. Phase 1 (get_reachability) showed 28 sampled pairs — including cross-domain probes from 10.5.0.x and 10.6.0.x hosts to all three Campus 1 subnets — at 0% packet loss with status "ok". Phase A infrastructure sweep (infra_sweep + l2_snapshot) revealed no ACL rules, no IP/gateway misconfigurations, no duplicate MACs, and all 15 hosts with valid addresses and default routes. Phase B control-plane sweep (ospf_snapshot + tc_snapshot) confirmed all 9 OSPF routers healthy: FRR daemons responding, every adjacency Full, 18 OSPF routes consistently present on each router, and no qdisc shaping anywhere. Phase D pressure sweep found no stress tools, CPU spikes, or socket saturation on any device. A targeted check on router16 specifically showed carrier-change counters at the startup-only baseline (2 transitions per interface), no flap or crash processes, no syslog entries, and a complete OSPF routing table that correctly contains all three Campus 1 prefixes via mswitch0. The "no default route" flag raised by dhcp_link_history is normal for an OSPF router with full prefix coverage and is not a fault. The reported symptom has no current manifestation, no historical trace, and no injected mechanism — it is an unconfirmed past or phantom incident.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes router16 is up with Full OSPF neighbors and forwards Campus 1 traffic (0% loss) at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly confirms router16 has Full OSPF adjacencies and that probes from off-campus to Campus 1 succeed with 0% packet loss, indicating baseline healthy forwarding.

The agent's claims are directly supported by the logged observations (reachability tests, OSPF snapshot, routing table, carrier-change counters, and syslog checks). The inferences follow logically and the investigation covers the essential checks to rule out a real or intermittent router failure.
